newsitem.title: JAPAN: Oversupply of DRAM chips to linger - analyst.
newsitem.headline: Oversupply of DRAM chips to linger - analyst.

text.p: The oversupply of dynamic random access memory (DRAM) chips is likely to continue for some time, an analyst at a brokerage-affiliated research firm said on Tuesday.
Although demand for the chips has been rising, supply is growing at a faster pace, said Akira Sato, analyst at New Japan Securities Research Institute.
Sato said the supply of DRAM chips has doubled from a year ago, but demand has lagged behind, going up by about 70 percent.
As a result, DRAM prices have fallen and are likely to decline further as the surplus is expected to continue to grow at a high rate, the analyst said.

The Japanese business daily Nihon Keizai Shimbun reported on Tuesday that standard 16-megabit DRAM chips are now traded in overseas spot markets at $6.20-$6.30, down more than 10 percent from the end of December.
But Sato said the oversupply problem should not hurt the stock prices of chip-related companies.

One of the reasons for the optimism is the expectation that the personal computer market will resume its high growth with the introduction of personal computers using Intel Corp's new MMX Pentium processors, Sato said.
